artifacts.summary: Design research for a merge_targets.mcp deploy-engine mechanism (mirroring the existing settings merge path) plus a verified finding that the absorbed obsidian-memory sub-task's declared npm package does not exist and the real plugin connects via Claude Code's native /ide integration, not .mcp.json.

next_steps: Run /orchestrate 29 to create an implementation plan from this research.

user_decision.question: The memory extension's declared obsidian-memory server (npx -y @anthropic-ai/obsidian-claude-code-mcp@latest) names an npm package that does not exist (confirmed 404 on the npm registry). The real plugin by that project name connects to Claude Code only through the native /ide integration, not through .mcp.json/npx at all. How should the absorbed 'register obsidian-memory' half of this task be resolved?
options: Drop the npx/.mcp.json wiring for obsidian-memory entirely; document Claude Code's native /ide integration as the real connection path in the memory extension README, and ship the merge_targets.mcp mechanism without a working obsidian-memory entry

Register a different, genuinely npm-published Obsidian MCP server (e.g. obsidian-mcp or @huangyihe/obsidian-mcp) under the obsidian-memory name instead, accepting its tool surface differs from what the task description assumed
Leave the obsidian-memory declaration as-is (non-functional) and only ship the generic merge_targets.mcp mechanism, deferring the obsidian fix to a follow-up task
user_decision.recommended: Drop the npx/.mcp.json wiring for obsidian-memory entirely; document Claude Code's native /ide integration as the real connection path in the memory extension README, and ship the merge_targets.mcp mechanism without a working obsidian-memory entry

memory_candidates.content: In this repo's extension deploy engine (lua/neotex/plugins/ai/shared/extensions/), merge_targets keys fall into two different idioms: 'settings' and 'index' are additive/tracked (merge_settings/unmerge_settings, append_index_entries/remove_index_entries_tracked) and preserve hand-written content; 'claudemd' and 'opencode_json' are fully computed artifacts regenerated wholesale on every load/unload (generate_claudemd/generate_opencode_json) and do NOT preserve hand-written content. A new merge_targets key should deliberately pick one idiom based on whether hand-edit preservation matters, not default to whichever is closer in the file.

Before trusting a manifest-declared MCP server command (npx package name, env var names) in this repo's extensions, verify the package actually exists (npm registry API, e.g. curl registry.npmjs.org/<pkg>) rather than assuming prior documentation is accurate. At least one existing declaration (obsidian-memory in the memory extension) named a non-existent @anthropic-ai npm package; the real project behind the name was an Obsidian plugin reachable only via Claude Code's native /ide integration, a completely different registration mechanism than .mcp.json/~/.claude.json.
